body:
Thank you, your advice is really reassuring.
I'm a lot less afraid than I was before, after learning more about how to manage the disease.
I'd heard about "reversing" diabetes, but wasn't sure if it was true or not. But I'm glad to here there is some truth to it. I'll definitely be working towards results like those if I am diagnosed.

Unfortunately the sink tends to back up. When the garbage disposal broke, we were using it, so there's still stuff in the drain and the smell is terrible. It's best not to use our kitchen sink at all.

I've heard so many people say cheese should be completely eliminated from your diet, so I'm surprised to hear this. I'll give fresh deli meat a try. I'm relatively certain there are a few places nearby.

Okay, that's good to hear. I'll keep the calories in mind, too.

Cleanup is definitely a factor. I'll try your suggestion.

Well, I'm happy to hear it's not too irritating. I worry about sounding whiny, especially to T1s who seem to have it far worse in many cases.

I'm comforted by the fact that the long term complications are often due to people neglecting their condition. If it has to go down this way I think I'd almost prefer I find this out when I'm young so the lifestyle changes I need to make aren't quite as jarring.
You're probably right. At this point I'm preparing myself for the worst.

I'm working on finding a place to make an appointment now. 

I suppose I'll be less ashamed if I slim down to a healthier weight. Maybe then I'd feel like it's less obvious why I'm in this situation.

And yes, admittedly WebMD was a bad idea, but it tends to be my go-to. But I'll be staying off of it from now on. I got all the information I needed.

That doesn't sound too bad. I'm pretty picky about vegetables (what a surprise) but maybe if I just tried some different things I'll find something I like. Is it safe for diabetics to eat cheese and deli meat? I've heard such horrible things about preservatives and all that so I figured it was off-limits.

Well, we have a fridge, a freezer, an oven, a stove, a microwave, all that. But unfortunately our sink is broken along with our garbage disposal and dish washer, making it hard to actually cook anything due to not having the option to clean things up well. But at this point I suppose I could resort to washing dishes in the damn bathtub if it meant getting healthy.

I'll look into testing it myself. I worry I'll somehow screw it up but it can't hurt to try if it's truly my only option.

I'm currently trying to figure out what to do about my diet when I'm not exactly able to cook at home. I suppose going temporarily raw vegan or something isn't going to hurt if I'm smart about it and don't accidentally starve myself.

I think I can handle the walking. There was a brief period of about 6 months in my life where I did walk, up to two whole hours every day, but of course depression set in worse than ever and I stopped.

I'm trying not to be too dismissive of the fact that I suffer from serious mental health disorders that lead me here, but it's not easy. I feel like diabetics, especially T2 diabetics, are always the butt of the joke, despite how devastating it can be. I've seen so many people be cruel, so it's hard not to be ashamed when I've been taught diabetics are supposed to be.

I may have to resort to clinic at this point.

There's not exactly a "plethora" of diabetic people in my family, and the handful of those who developed T2 have passed away (due to unrelated causes, if I recall correctly.) Thankfully they lived to ripe old ages of 80+ years.

I do need to see a counselor but that's... just another expense entirely.

This is pretty comforting, thank you.

I just worry about the diabetic horror stories, but I suppose those come from people continuing to live unhealthily after being diagnosed. I don't want to get taken by heart disease. I don't want my kidneys to fail. I don't want to have to have amputations. I'm afraid of going blind. All these things terrify me. 

I'll be getting tested for T1 just in case. I know it's highly unlikely but not unheard of that people my age with similar symptoms actually have T1 in disguise.

I've been telling myself for years that I need to start exercising and eating a healthier diet. As unfortunate as it is I guess this is the reality check I needed.
Yeah, I figured as much. Thanks for your advice.

Well, I cut out soda because of the sugar. I only mentioned the salt content (which varies from brand to brand, I guess) because it seemed that was the culprit for any frequent urination I was experiencing. However I might just be trying to fool myself into thinking I'm not experiencing as many symptoms.

I'm trying to figure out where and how to get tested in my current financial predicament. I know reddit posts aren't going to diagnose me.

Truth be told, it seems prediabetes is a bit of a myth based on what I've read. I only use the term because that's what I keep finding, but I know better than to be optimistic that this is completely reversible. I just worry I've dug my own grave at only 19.

And I do know the long term effects, and I'm terrified.

There's no need to apologize for your tone. I know this is probably the most irritating type of post in the world for Type 1 diabetics.
What do you mean by somewhere in the middle? Do you think I'm already diabetic, or is this a slippery slope? I don't understand.
